A B S T R A C T
In recent years, distributed scheduling problems have been well studied for their close connection with multi-
factory production networks. However, the maintenance operations that are commonly carried out on a sys
tem to restore it to a specific state are seldom taken into consideration. In this paper, we study a distributed
permutation flowshop scheduling problem with preventive maintenance operation (PM/DPFSP). A multi-start
iterated greedy (MSIG) algorithm is proposed to minimize the makespan. An improved heuristic is presented
for the initialization and re-initialization by adding a dropout operation to NEH2 to generate solutions with a
high level of quality and disperstiveness. A destruction phase with the tournament selection and a construction
phase with an enhanced strategy are introduced to avoid local optima. A local search based on three effective
operators is integrated into the MSIG to reinforce local neighborhood solution exploitation. In addition. a restart
strategy is adpoted if a solution has not been improved in a certain number of consecutive iterations. We con
ducted extensive experiments to test the performance of the presented MSIG. The computational results indicate
that the presented MSIG has many promising advantages in solving the PM/DPFSP under consideration.

narrow the gap between academic research and practical applications,
DPFSP has been studied for a long time as an extension of the permu
tation flowshop scheduling problem (Maccarthy and Liu, 1993). Naderi

many authors have studied more advanced algorithms in the last de

(2011) to minimize the maximum completion time, where an efficient
local search was utilized to explore neighboring solutions. Gao, Chen
and Deng (2013) proposed a tabu algorithm with a novel tabu strategy.

Huang (2013) modified the iterated greedy (IG) algorithm for the
DPFSP. and proposed a destruction operator with a variable number of
removed jobs and a simulated annealing algorithm with a sinking tem
perature. Wang et al. (2013) proposed an effective estimation of distri.
bution algorithm (EDA). They employed the earliest completion factory
rule, and designed a probability model, and proposed four local search
operators based on the problem characteristics. Naderi and Ruiz (2014)
presented a scatter search (SS) procedure, which has seldom been

statistically outperform the other 11 algorithms in the experiments. Xu
et al. (201 4) proposed a hybrid immune algorithm, where four different
local search operators were used in a hybrid way within the frame of the
immune algorithm. Fernandez-Viagas and Framinan (2015) developed a
bounded-search IG algorithm for the DPESP In order to reduce the
number of solutions to be evaluated. they studied the property of the
problem to estimate the makespan of a factory when a new job is

tational time is discarded by 32.31% and the number of iterations is
decreased by 11.68%. Bargaoui, Belkahla Driss and Gh´edira (2017)
presented a chemical reaction optimization algorithm, in which a one
point crossover and a greedy strategy are embedded to ameliorate the
solution quality. Deng and Wang (2017) proposed a competitive mem:
etic algorithm to solve the multi-objective DPFSP with makespan and
total tardiness criteria. They employed two populations to optimize the
two objectives and designed the interaction between the two pop
ulations to balance the two obiectives. Ruiz. Pan and Naderi (2019)
presented a simple two-stage iterated greedy (IG2S) algorithm with
improved initialization, destruction, construction and local search

total flowtime optimization, Fernandezviagas, Perezgonzalez and Fra

presented a hybrid discrete differential evolution (DDE) algorithm to
deal with the distributed blocking flowshop scheduling problem

distributed assembly permutation flowshop scheduling problem in
which each factory consists of a flowshop for part-processing and an
assembly line for product-processing. Meng, Pan and Wang (2019)

with the DPFSP with due windows to minimize the total weighted

4. The proposed multi-start iterated greedy algorithm
In the literature, a high performing heuristic is often used to initialize
the search for an IG algorithm. The main loop is to greedily repeat four
operations (Ruiz & Stützle, 2007; Ruiz, Pan & Naderi, 2019):
Utilize the destruction to partially destroy the candidate solution. For
our problem, some jobs will be removed from the solution, resulting
in an incomplete solution and a group of leftover jobs.
Apply a greedy heuristic method to reinsert the removed jobs into the
solution. A new complete solution will be generated in this con
struction phase.
Perform a local search to further optimize the new solution.
Use a simulated annealing-like acceptance criterion with a constant
temperature to determine whether the new solution is accepted.

neighborhood structure, the swap and insertion operators are widely
used in the local search phase (Fernandezviagas, Valente & Framinan,

Inter-factory Swap Local Search (ISLS): We test to swap each job in

6. Conclusions and future research
Distributed scheduling in multi-factory production has been a hot
research topic in the past decades. However, scheduling problems with

Then the algorithm restarts with the heuristic method. We carried out

not take full advantage of existing solutions. We are going to further
study the restarting method to promote efficiency. In addition, we are
also interested in other objectives in PM/DPFSP (e.g. total flow time,
total tardiness) which are common in practice.
